questions.e: Terms of trade measure the rate at which exports exchange for imports, so an improvement means export prices have risen relative to import prices. It says nothing directly about volumes or the overall balance.

questions.s: A tax placed on imported goods is called
questions.e: A tariff raises the price of imports to protect home producers or raise revenue. A quota limits the quantity of imports, and an excise duty is a tax on goods produced at home.

questions.s: A limit on the physical quantity of a good that may be imported in a year is
questions.e: A quota fixes the amount allowed in, whatever the price. A tariff works through price instead, by taxing each unit imported.

questions.s: Selling a good abroad at a price below the price charged in the home market, or below its cost, is called
questions.e: Dumping can harm producers in the importing country, which may respond with anti-dumping duties. Devaluation is a deliberate reduction in a currency's fixed exchange rate.

questions.s: The infant industry argument is used to justify
o: temporary protection of new domestic industries
removal of all tariffs on imports
permanent free trade in all goods
questions.e: A new industry may need protection until it grows large enough to reach economies of scale and compete with established foreign firms. The argument supports protection only for a limited time.

questions.s: The balance of trade records a country's
o: exports and imports of goods and services
all transactions with the rest of the world
exports and imports of goods only
questions.e: The balance of trade (visible balance) covers merchandise trade only. The balance of payments records all economic transactions, including services, incomes, transfers and capital flows.

questions.s: Which item is recorded in the current account of the balance of payments?
o: A foreign loan taken by the government
Remittances sent home by workers abroad
Repayment of the principal of a foreign loan
Purchase of shares by a foreign company
questions.e: The current account includes trade in goods and services, primary income and current transfers such as workers' remittances. Loans, share purchases and loan repayments are capital and financial account items.

questions.s: Earnings from tourists, shipping and insurance services sold to foreigners are called
questions.e: Services cannot be seen crossing the border, so they are invisible items in the current account. Visible exports are physical goods such as rice and textiles.

questions.s: A country's exports of goods are Rs 400 billion, imports of goods Rs 550 billion, net services Rs −30 billion, net primary income Rs −20 billion and current transfers Rs 180 billion. Its current account balance is
questions.e: Current account = (400 − 550) − 30 − 20 + 180 = −150 − 50 + 180 = −20, a deficit of Rs 20 billion. A deficit of Rs 150 billion is only the trade balance.

questions.s: The balance of payments always balances in an accounting sense because
o: exports always equal imports in value each year
the exchange rate is always fixed
every transaction is recorded by double entry
questions.e: Each transaction appears as a credit and a matching debit, so the accounts sum to zero once reserves and errors and omissions are included. A current account deficit must be financed by a capital or financial inflow or by using reserves.

questions.s: The rate at which one currency is exchanged for another is called
questions.e: An exchange rate is the price of one currency in terms of another, for example rupees per US dollar. The terms of trade compare export and import prices.

questions.s: Under a freely floating exchange rate system, the exchange rate is determined by
o: the demand for and supply of the currency
the central bank at a fixed level set by law
questions.e: In a floating system, market forces set the rate: exports and capital inflows create demand for the currency, imports and outflows create supply. A rate kept at a set level by the authorities is a fixed system.

questions.s: The rupee falls from Rs 200 to Rs 250 per US dollar. A Pakistani exporter sells cloth abroad at Rs 1,000 a metre. The dollar price of the cloth
o: falls from 5 dollars to 2.50 dollars a metre
falls from 5 dollars to 4 dollars a metre
rises from 4 dollars to 5 dollars a metre
questions.e: At Rs 200 per dollar the cloth costs 1,000 ÷ 200 = 5 dollars; at Rs 250 per dollar it costs 1,000 ÷ 250 = 4 dollars. A weaker rupee makes Pakistani goods cheaper abroad and so helps exports.

questions.s: A fall in the value of a currency under a floating exchange rate is called
questions.e: Depreciation is a market-driven fall; devaluation is a deliberate cut in the official rate under a fixed system. Appreciation is a rise in value.

questions.s: Depreciation of a country's currency is most likely to
o: make its exports dearer and its imports cheaper
lower the price of imported oil at home
make its exports cheaper and its imports dearer
reduce the foreign debt in home currency
questions.e: A weaker currency lowers foreign prices of exports and raises home prices of imports, which can improve the trade balance over time. It raises, not lowers, the home-currency cost of foreign debt and imported oil.

questions.s: According to the purchasing power parity theory, exchange rates in the long run adjust so that
o: every country has a trade surplus
a currency buys the same basket of goods in each country
exports always equal imports in volume
interest rates are equal in every country
questions.e: PPP says the exchange rate moves to equalise the purchasing power of currencies: if prices at home rise faster than abroad, the home currency depreciates. It is a long-run tendency, not an exact daily rule.

questions.s: Which policy would help reduce a deficit in the current account of the balance of payments?
o: Raising tariffs on imported luxury goods
Raising the exchange value of the currency
questions.e: Higher tariffs make imports dearer and reduce spending on them. Removing duties, a stronger currency or more spending on imports would all widen the deficit.

questions.s: The canon of economy in taxation means that
o: the tax rate should never change
taxes should take more from the rich
taxes should be paid when income is received
the cost of collecting a tax should be small
questions.e: Adam Smith argued that a tax costing a large share of its yield to collect is wasteful. Paying when income is received is the canon of convenience, and taxing according to ability to pay is equality.

questions.s: A tax of 10 % is charged on all incomes, whatever their size. Such a tax is
questions.e: A single rate for every income takes the same percentage from rich and poor, so it is proportional. A progressive tax would have rising rates for higher incomes.

questions.s: The incidence of a tax refers to
o: the person who finally bears the burden of the tax
the total revenue the tax raises
the person on whom the tax is first imposed by law
the rate at which the tax is charged
questions.e: Impact is on the person who first pays the tax to the government; incidence is on whoever finally bears it after any shifting. For an indirect tax the seller bears the impact, but much of the incidence may fall on buyers.

questions.s: Government spending on roads, schools and hospitals is called
questions.e: Development (capital) expenditure builds assets that raise future output. Debt servicing is payment of interest and principal on past loans, and current revenue is income such as taxes.

questions.s: Public finance is the branch of economics that studies
o: the behaviour of individual consumers and households
the trade of a country with others
the income and expenditure of the government
questions.e: Public finance deals with government revenue (taxes, borrowing), public expenditure and public debt. Banking and international trade are separate branches.

questions.s: A non-tax source of revenue for a government is
questions.e: Non-tax revenue includes profits of public enterprises, fees, fines and interest on government loans. Income tax, customs duty and sales tax are all taxes.

questions.s: When the central bank lowers the cash reserve ratio from 10 % to 5 %, the maximum credit multiplier
questions.e: Multiplier = 1 ÷ r: 1 ÷ 0.10 = 10 and 1 ÷ 0.05 = 20. A lower reserve ratio lets banks lend more of each deposit, so the multiplier rises.

questions.s: Bank deposits that can be transferred by cheque and are accepted in payment are called
questions.e: Bank deposits that can be transferred by cheque or electronically are bank money, created by commercial banks. Full-bodied money has a material value equal to its face value.

questions.s: Free trade between countries is generally expected to
o: raise the prices paid by consumers
protect every domestic industry from loss
end the need for any exchange rate
questions.e: When each country specialises in goods of comparative advantage, total output rises and consumers get cheaper goods. Some domestic industries lose, which is why free trade has critics.

questions.s: A country has a balance of payments deficit. Which of these would directly finance it?
o: Increasing its imports of machinery and oil
Drawing on its foreign exchange reserves
questions.e: A deficit means more foreign currency is going out than coming in, so it must be met by using reserves or by borrowing abroad. Higher imports would add to the deficit.

questions.s: Which of the following creates a demand for Pakistani rupees in the foreign exchange market?
o: Foreign buyers paying for Pakistani rice
Pakistani firms buying machinery from abroad
questions.e: Foreigners need rupees to pay for Pakistani exports, so exports create demand for the rupee. Imports, fees paid abroad and outbound tourism supply rupees in exchange for foreign currency.

questions.s: If a central bank buys government securities from commercial banks, the likely effect is
o: an increase in bank reserves and lending
an immediate rise in interest rates
a fall in the money supply
a decrease in bank reserves and in bank lending
questions.e: The central bank pays for the securities by crediting banks' reserve accounts, so banks have more to lend and the money supply rises. Selling securities has the opposite effect.

questions.s: A cheque is a written order by a depositor to his bank to
o: lend him money at a fixed rate of interest
change his rupees into foreign currency
pay a stated sum to the person named on it
keep his valuables safely in a locker
questions.e: A cheque instructs the bank to pay a named payee, or the bearer, from the drawer's account. Lending, lockers and foreign exchange are other bank services, not what a cheque does.

questions.s: The credit-creating power of commercial banks is larger when
o: people hold more cash outside the banks
the cash reserve ratio is higher
banks keep more excess reserves idle
the cash reserve ratio is lower
questions.e: A smaller required reserve means each deposit supports more lending, so the multiplier 1 ÷ r is larger. Cash held by the public and idle excess reserves are leakages that reduce credit creation.

questions.s: When the central bank lends to a commercial bank in difficulty to prevent a bank failure, it acts as
questions.e: As lender of last resort the central bank supplies funds to sound banks facing a sudden shortage of cash, protecting the whole banking system. Holding the country's foreign exchange reserves is another, separate function.

questions.s: Trade between two different countries is called
questions.e: International (foreign) trade crosses national borders and involves different currencies. Internal trade takes place within one country, between its regions.
